text:
maria: Quick sync — we need a crisp rubric for model entry+sunset that sales can sign up customers against. Thinking lightweight so we can move faster.
aj: +1. What are non-negotiables? latency pctiles, embed drift, and a minimal eval pass?
san: I'd add a customer migration window expectation. Call it a 'twilight window' — e.g., 90 days from deprecation notice. Customers get migration credits during that period.
lina: Love the 'twilight' term. Also should we require a canary lane for 1 week at production QPS before GA?
em: For benchmarks, propose: 95th-percentile latency under target, embed cosine recall >= 0.85 on key slices, and smoke LLM safety checks (no regressions on the guard prompts).
maria: Draft rubric idea: 1) Basic perf: p95 latency, mem/kv footprint; 2) Quality: bench slices pass; 3) Stability: 1-week canary at 20% traffic; 4) Migration contract: twilight window + compat shim if needed. Thoughts?
aj: Maybe make the canary requirement conditional based on model family — small LMs <=6B get faster path.
sam: Also add a pin/rollback policy: default pin TTL = 30 days after GA unless customer opts into longer. We need clarity for enterprise.
lina: Customers often ask for hard pins. Proposal: default auto-rotate, but offer paid pin exceptions with SLA. Document the onramp for those.
em: On the deprecation side: sequence = Notice -> Migration credits -> Compatibility shim (if feasible) -> Sunset after twilight. Tooling: make a migration tracker tile in the Console.
ops-bot: Deploy reminder: canary lane infra tickets required. Ticket template: `CANARY-REQ - model, qps, start_ts, end_ts, fallback-model`.
maria: For acceptance benchmarks, let's keep a short required eval set (10-20 representative prompts) + a heavier regression suite run in CI. If the heavy suite fails, hold GA and schedule engineering triage.
aj: Who owns the representative prompts? Should be a joint effort: Product + SE + Customer (if they opt in).
sam: Question: how strict is the embed recall floor? 0.85 might be tough for some families. Maybe use relative baseline vs current default model on that tenant slice, e.g., no worse than -5% relative.
lina: Good call. Make bench rules: either absolute floor OR relative delta vs baseline.
em: We should add a 'rollback gate' metric: if customer-facing error rate > X or latency SLO breaches > Y for >Z minutes during canary, auto-roll back. Define X/Y/Z.
maria: Propose X = 1% user-visible errors, Y = p95 > 2x target for 15m. Ops to confirm.
aj: Implementation notes: 1) Add fields to model-catalog manifest: `twilight_window_days`, `canary_qps`, `pin_ttl_days`, `compat_shim` boolean. 2) Console: new 'migration' tab.
sam: Customer messaging: standardized deprecation email + migration playbook. Sales wants templated comms and a checkbox in the contract for paid pin exceptions.
lina: For internal prioritization, tie onboarding SLA to expected revenue bucket. Low-rev models get a faster but lighter acceptance path.
em: Any objections to a 2-track onboarding: Fastpath (minimal checks, >10k monthly users cap) vs Fullpath (canary + heavy bench + enterprise pin options)?
maria: I like it. Fastpath for experiments/early dev, Fullpath for production and enterprise. Document gating thresholds.
aj: Next steps: someone from Product to write the first draft rubric doc, Eng to map canary infra, Legal/Sales to sketch contract language for pin exceptions. Owners?
maria: I'll take the draft rubric. @aj can you own the canary infra mapping? @sam handle the migration credits model? @lina coordinate Sales/Legal contract language?
aj: Yep, will do.
sam: I'll prototype migration credit math and a small template for the Console migration tile.
lina: Will draft contract language and sample comms.
em: I'll help define the regression suites and monitoring gates.
ops-bot: Note created: `TASK-4882` model lifecycle rubric draft assigned to maria, due in 5d.
maria: Thanks — aiming to share a PR in 4 days. If anyone has friction items, flag here. :thumbsup:
